key_insight: HTP-Net improves instance segmentation of dense, slender welding material stubs by preserving boundaries, modeling long-range topology, and using orientation-aware predictions.
engineering_relevance: More reliable stub counting and shape measurement can support automated inventory management in welding factories.
method: Wavelet-Driven Edge-Preserving module retains subtle boundaries during downsampling.
Long-Range Topology Representation Block models global context to reduce fragmentation of slender targets.
Orientation-Driven Instance Segmentation Head uses rotational priors to reduce excessive non-maximum suppression and overlapping masks.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports mAP50 gains of 1.2%–55.3% over existing methods on custom and public datasets, plus factory-deployed average recognition accuracies of 99% for electrode stubs and 94% for wire stubs.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify dataset sizes, inference speed, or robustness across factory conditions, leaving deployment generalizability uncertain.
paper_title: High-resolution topology-preserving instance segmentation network for vision-based measurement system of dense welding material stubs
